title: VTE prophylaxis in surgical patients
subject: anaesthesia
setting: Surgical wards, pre-assessment, orthopaedics, day surgery
summary: Assess VTE and bleeding risk on admission (Caprini score), start mechanical prophylaxis, add LMWH or UFH when VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk, and extend prophylaxis to 28 days after major abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery and to 4 to 5 weeks after hip arthroplasty or hip fracture.

sections.title: Assess VTE and bleeding risk
items: Assess every surgical patient on admission or by first consultant review, and reassess after surgery or any clinical change.
Caprini score (ACCP 2012): 0 very low (under 0.5% VTE risk), 1 to 2 low (about 1.5%), 3 to 4 moderate (about 3%), 5 or more high (about 6%).

Risk factors: surgery over 90 minutes (over 60 minutes if pelvic or lower limb), cancer, previous VTE, thrombophilia, age over 60, obesity, immobility, oestrogen therapy, pregnancy or postpartum, arthroplasty, hip fracture, major trauma.

High bleeding risk: active bleeding, acquired or inherited bleeding disorder, platelets under 75 x 10^9/L, uncontrolled hypertension, recent intracranial haemorrhage, neurosurgery or spinal surgery, concurrent anticoagulants.
Advise stopping oestrogen-containing contraceptives or HRT 4 weeks before elective major surgery, with alternative contraception.

sections.title: General, abdominal and pelvic surgery
items: Very low risk: early ambulation only. Low risk: mechanical prophylaxis, preferably intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC).
Moderate or high risk without high bleeding risk: LMWH or low-dose UFH; add mechanical prophylaxis for high risk. IPC is preferred over graduated stockings (ASH 2019).
NICE: start mechanical prophylaxis on admission for abdominal surgery and add LMWH (or fondaparinux) for at least 7 days when VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk.
Extend LMWH to 28 days after major abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery.
High bleeding risk: mechanical prophylaxis (IPC) until bleeding risk falls, then add pharmacological prophylaxis.
Bariatric surgery: mechanical plus LMWH for at least 7 days; use weight-adjusted LMWH doses per local protocol.

sections.title: Orthopaedic surgery
items: Elective hip replacement (NICE): LMWH for 10 days then aspirin 75 or 150 mg for 28 days, or LMWH for 28 days with stockings until discharge, or rivaroxaban; apixaban or dabigatran if these cannot be used.
Elective knee replacement (NICE): aspirin 75 or 150 mg for 14 days, or LMWH for 14 days with stockings until discharge, or rivaroxaban; apixaban or dabigatran as alternatives.
ASH 2019 accepts aspirin or anticoagulants after arthroplasty, and if an anticoagulant is chosen suggests a DOAC over LMWH.

Hip fracture: LMWH starting 6 to 12 hours after surgery (or fondaparinux from 6 hours) for 1 month. If surgery is delayed beyond the day after admission, give pre-operative LMWH with the last dose at least 12 hours before surgery.
Knee arthroscopy under 90 minutes in low-risk patients usually needs no prophylaxis; lower limb immobilisation in a cast may need LMWH while immobilised.

sections.title: Timing and neuraxial anaesthesia
items: Start pharmacological prophylaxis as soon as possible and within 14 hours of the decision to admit, unless a procedure-specific timing applies.
LMWH can be started 12 hours or more before surgery or 12 hours or more after surgery (ACCP), or 6 to 12 hours after surgery (NICE hip fracture).
Plan LMWH timing around spinal or epidural anaesthesia: puncture or catheter removal at least 12 hours after a prophylactic dose, next dose at least 4 hours after catheter removal.
Regional anaesthesia itself lowers VTE risk versus general anaesthesia and can be considered alongside other prophylaxis.

sections.title: Special groups
items: Renal impairment (eGFR under 30 mL/min/1.73 m2): LMWH at reduced dose (enoxaparin 20 mg daily) or UFH 5000 units SC, following local protocol.
Obesity: consider higher, weight-adjusted LMWH doses per local protocol; mechanical prophylaxis must be correctly sized.
Pregnancy and up to 6 weeks postpartum: use the RCOG or local obstetric risk tool; LMWH is the agent of choice.
Patients on antiplatelet agents: consider pharmacological prophylaxis if VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk.
Heparin is of animal (porcine) origin; discuss alternatives such as fondaparinux or mechanical methods with patients who object.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Check platelets at baseline; if UFH is used or there has been heparin exposure in the last 100 days, monitor platelets for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (days 4 to 14).
Check stockings daily: do not use them with peripheral arterial disease, peripheral neuropathy, fragile skin, severe leg oedema or leg deformity.
Before discharge on extended prophylaxis: teach injection technique or give oral agent instructions, state the stop date, and inform the GP.
Educate on DVT and PE symptoms and when to seek help.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: No documented risk assessment, or no reassessment after surgery.
Stopping LMWH at discharge after major cancer surgery or hip arthroplasty when extended prophylaxis is indicated.
Giving LMWH too close to spinal or epidural puncture or catheter removal.
Full-dose LMWH in severe renal impairment without adjustment.
Graduated stockings on patients with peripheral arterial disease or neuropathy.

drugs.name: Enoxaparin
drugs.notes: 20 mg once daily if CrCl below 30 mL/min. Start 12 hours before or 6 to 12 hours after surgery. Widely available in India.

drugs.name: Unfractionated heparin
drugs.notes: Preferred in severe renal impairment; monitor platelets.

drugs.name: Fondaparinux
drugs.dose: 2.5 mg SC once daily, first dose 6 hours after surgery
drugs.notes: If LMWH contraindicated; avoid in severe renal impairment.

drugs.name: Rivaroxaban
drugs.dose: 10 mg orally once daily, starting 6 to 10 hours after surgery
drugs.notes: About 5 weeks after hip and 2 weeks after knee replacement.

drugs.name: Apixaban
drugs.dose: 2.5 mg orally twice daily, starting 12 to 24 hours after surgery
drugs.notes: 32 to 38 days after hip and 10 to 14 days after knee replacement.

drugs.name: Aspirin
drugs.notes: Knee replacement 14 days; after 10 days of LMWH for 28 days in hip replacement (NICE).
